item.title: “Good is restraint over the eye, Good is restraint over the ear, Good is restraint over the nose, Good is restraint over the tongue.” “Good…
item.description:
“Good is restraint over the eye,
Good is restraint over the ear,
Good is restraint over the nose,
Good is restraint over the tongue.”

“Good is restraint over the body,
Good is restraint over speech,
Good is restraint over the mind,
Good is restraint everywhere.
A monk restrained everywhere
Is freed from all suffering.”

“One who controls his hands and feet,
Controls his speech and his head,
Delights in inner seclusion,
Is content, lives alone —
Him they call a monk.”

From: Dhammapada 360-382

item.title: “Seeing the destruction of birth, The end of fetters, Destroying the path of sensual desire, Without remainder — That one is pure, faultless, Stainless, undefiled…
item.description:
“Seeing the destruction of birth,
The end of fetters,
Destroying the path of sensual desire,
Without remainder —
That one is pure, faultless,
Stainless, undefiled —
The Tathāgata is worthy of offerings.”

“One who does not see a self within the self,
Concentrated, upright, steady,
Without desire, without rigidity, without doubt —
The Tathāgata is worthy of offerings.”

“One in whom there is no root of delusion,
Who knows, who sees all things,
Who bears this last body —
Attaining perfect enlightenment,
The unsurpassed state of peace —
Thus is the Tathāgata, worthy of offerings.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.4

item.title: “Monks, what is Right Mindfulness? Monks, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow…
item.description:
“Monks, what is Right Mindfulness? Monks, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world. This, monks, is called Right Mindfulness.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Hemavata: “Is he without desire for sensual pleasures? Is his mind undisturbed? Has he overcome all delusion? Does he truly have eyes for all things?”…
item.description:
Hemavata:
“Is he without desire for sensual pleasures?
Is his mind undisturbed?
Has he overcome all delusion?
Does he truly have eyes for all things?”

Sātāgira:
“He has no desire for sensual pleasures,
His mind is undisturbed,
He has overcome all delusion —
The Buddha truly has eyes for all things.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.9

item.title: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and…
item.description:
“Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: ‘Good man, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may meet death or deadly suffering.’ That man might eat it without reflection, without refusal. While eating, he does not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he meets death or deadly suffering. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has painful results in the future.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 46 – Mahādhammasamādānasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained…
item.description:
“Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, not skilled in the true Dhamma, not trained in the true Dhamma, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. For him, that form changes and alters. Because of the change and alteration of form, his consciousness follows that change in form. Worrying states arise from that consciousness following the change in form, invading his mind and remaining. Because his mind is invaded, he is terrified, distressed, and full of longing and worry.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.7
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the…
item.description:
“Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and dwelt with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful. Then I saw other beings who had not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, being burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures. I did not envy them, nor did I delight in that. Why is that? Because, Māgandiya, there is this pleasure and rapture, apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states, and having attained the heavenly pleasure, I dwell delighting in that. I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta

item.title: “Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
item.description:
“Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Householder, a monk who has clinging does not attain complete Nibbāna … Households, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue … Householder, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because he delights, praises, and dwells with lust, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Having clinging, householder, that monk does not attain Nibbāna. This, householder, is the cause, this is the reason why some beings here and now do not attain complete Nibbāna.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.124
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a…
item.description:
“Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a hiding place near the bait cast by Māra and the world’s offerings. Having made a hiding place, without entering, without indulging, we will eat the bait and the world’s offerings. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become infatuated; not infatuated, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not become subject to Māra’s will among that bait and offerings.’ These ascetics and brahmins make a hiding place near the bait and offerings. Having done so, without entering, without indulging, they eat the bait and offerings. Not entering, not indulging, they do not become infatuated; not infatuated, they do not become heedless; not heedless, they do not become subject to Māra’s will. But then they have such wrong views as: ‘The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite …’ Thus, monks, these third ascetics and brahmins have not escaped Māra’s power.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 25 – Nivāpasutta

item.title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? What does a person rely on? - Craving gives birth to…
item.description:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
What does a person rely on?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Kamma is what a person relies on.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.57
